result.summary: Fixes a bug the author introduced in #31551 where BufferedWriter's destructor retries a failed write during exception unwinding, triggering std::terminate instead of normal error handling. The fix clears the pending byte count in flush() before writing so the destructor cannot retry, and adds explicit flush() calls in BlockManager::WriteBlock/WriteBlockUndo before the buffered writer is destroyed. A regression test reproduces the double-write-on-failed-flush scenario.
result.problem: When local storage fails mid-write (e.g. a full disk while writing a block or undo record), the implicit destructor-triggered retry throws inside a noexcept destructor, causing bitcoind to abort via std::terminate rather than reporting a clean storage error and shutting down gracefully. This affects node operators and anyone running nodes on storage that can fill up, as the author observed on their own benchmarking servers.

result.card: This PR fixes a bug the author introduced in #31551 where BufferedWriter's destructor retries a failed write during exception unwinding, turning a recoverable storage error into an uncontrolled std::terminate/abort. The fix clears pending bytes in flush() before writing and makes BlockManager::WriteBlock/WriteBlockUndo flush explicitly before their buffered writer is destroyed, restoring normal storage-error handling and clean shutdown. Evidence: author reproduced the abort on a real filesystem-full scenario ('my 1 TB benchmarking servers have recently been filling up') and included a manual reproducer showing exit 134 (abort) versus exit 1 (handled) after the fix. Reviewer w0xlt independently hit the same bug and gave a Concept ACK, sharing an alternative fix; andrewtoth's question about severity was answered by the author, and maflcko raised only a broader non-blocking wish for a systemic pattern. The PR is small, tested, mergeable, and has no dependency on other open PRs.
